title: CI runs the macOS legs on every push and never cancels a run that a newer push has superseded
body:
`.github/workflows/tests.yml` runs on every push to `main` and on every pull request, with no `concurrency` block and with both macOS legs on every push: a run that a newer push has superseded still runs to the end, and macOS runs whether or not anything will read it.

THE RULING, hv, 2026-09-21, for the fleet (Devbin issue 0108, Devbin vc decision 32): (1) a macOS job runs only on release tags and on demand, in every repository with macOS artefacts, and Ubuntu stays on every push; (2) every repository cancels superseded runs on push, not only the macOS ones.

AT UTILZ, BOTH HALVES, and the record of how that was settled, because the first commit here cites the other answer. cc put a case to hv at 07:38Z that Utilz should take half (2) alone: the repository is public (`gh repo view matthewsinclair/utilz` reads PUBLIC), GitHub charges nothing for standard hosted runners there, macOS included, the minutes behind the ruling were measured across the private repositories only (Devbin 0108), and the macOS legs are Utilz's only bash 3.2 run, so gating them puts the first 3.2 run after the core has pushed the tag. hv answered "Yes" to that. Between 07:40Z and 07:50Z, with the same argument in front of it through devbin's own node, hv ruled the other way and uniformly: "Keep things uniform, regardless of public/private repo state", and, put again as a choice in cc's session with both consequences, "Uniform fleet rule applies here" (cc read `date -u` at 09:09Z, immediately after). **The uniform ruling is the one in force**, and the 07:38Z answer is superseded rather than forgotten: it is recorded here because its reasoning is the cost of the ruling, and because the bash 3.2 gap it names is real and is closed in the release gate instead (vc).

THE FIX, in `tests.yml` unless named:

- A workflow-level `concurrency` block, its group keyed on the workflow, the EVENT NAME and `github.ref`, with `cancel-in-progress: true`. A newer push cancels the run on `main` that it supersedes; a manual run and a push on one ref do not cancel each other; a pull request is a group of its own.
- `test-macos` runs only on `github.ref_type == 'tag' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`, and the `rust` job carries the same condition IN ITS MATRIX, because a job-level `if` would drop its Ubuntu leg with it.
- `on.push` gains both tag forms, `['v[0-9]*', '[0-9]*']`: this project's tags are bare from 2.7.0 on. Nothing reads the tag's text, since both gates test `ref_type`, so the form cannot silently exclude a release. `workflow_dispatch` is added for the on-demand half.
- `on.push` gains `paths-ignore: ['intent/whiteboard/**']`, so a push that only moves the board runs nothing. Path filters are not evaluated for a tag push, so this can never suppress a release run.
- **`test-summary` is rewritten, and it is the half that bites.** It required `needs.test-macos.result == 'success'` unconditionally, so gating the legs without touching it turns every push red, on the NEXT push rather than on the commit that did it (measured at Molt, through devbin). The results now arrive as `env` data rather than as script text; `MACOS_REQUIRED` carries the same expression as `test-macos`'s own `if`, so the gate and the leg cannot disagree about when macOS runs; macOS is required on a tag or a manual run, `success` or `skipped` is accepted otherwise, and anything else, an empty or unrecognised result included, fails.
- `test-summary` runs on `!cancelled()` rather than `always()`. `always()` is true in a cancelled run too, so once cancelling is routine every superseded run would start the summary, which exits 1 and reports the cancelled jobs as failed tests.
- Actions pinned to the versions the fleet pass names, in `tests.yml` and `pr-checks.yml`: `actions/checkout@v7.0.1`, `actions/setup-node@v7.0.0`.

`pr-checks.yml` gains no concurrency block: it runs on pull requests only, and Utilz commits straight to `main`.

WHAT IT CHANGES DOWNSTREAM: a superseded commit's run now concludes `cancelled`, routinely rather than by hand. `utilz install` and `upgrade` record CI's verdict and never enforce it (install.sh:894-896), so a publish from such a commit records `cancelled`. `tools/ci-state`, the release core's `ci.query`, reads `cancelled` as `failed`. A release commit can only meet that if something lands on `main` between the release push and the core's CI read, which the cut's hold on every write (ST0019 D6) already rules out. **And a release commit now carries TWO runs**, one for the branch push and one for the tag, where only the tag's carries macOS; `install_ci_state` asks for one run (`--limit 1`, install.sh:674), so which of the two it reads is not settled by this issue. `docs/releasing.md` says what CI covers on a push and on a tag.

TESTS: none added. The blocks are configuration GitHub reads, and the proof is CI's own run on the pushed commit, green, with the shape checks that already read `tests.yml` (`opt/utilz/test/common_lib.bats`) still passing.
